- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is negative or mixed (especially after recent spikes).  
- Underestimate sharp downward moves after strong positive sentiment spikes — model tends to overreact to recent highs.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, reduce forecasted mean by 2–5% to account for mean reversion.  
- Avoid over-optimistic 30-day forecasts after 10+ consecutive days of price decline — model often fails to recognize exhaustion.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak, model tends to overshoot — cap forecast peak at 10–15% above recent high.  
- Lagged price drops (e.g., 3–5 day delay) are often missed — adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lagged decline if sentiment shows weakening.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often overestimates upside — reduce forecast by 3–7% for 10+ day horizons.
